Maria (People Ops): Quick question — offer accepted by Arpita but she says she plans to concurrently file I-485 + I-765. She asked if she can still start 2026-05-01 and enroll in benefits while filing. Any blocking issues? cc @Priya (immigration)
Ash (Hiring Manager): Would love her to start then, full-time. We can be flexible on on-site date if docs are pending.
Arpita (Candidate): Thanks! I should have my receipts for I-485/I-765 within a few weeks after filing. I wanted to check whether that receipt lets me get benefits before the physical EAD arrives.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Short answer: a receipt for I-485 alone does not grant work authorization. The I-765 (EAD) application can be filed concurrently; the EAD receipt (Form I-797C) can sometimes be used for I-9 'receipt rule' purposes to show authorization to work for 240 days, but that depends on the specific I-9 employer guidance and current USCIS policy.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Also note USCIS processing times vary — EAD can be 3–6+ months. Advanced Parole (I-131) separate. If the candidate needs to physically travel, AP matters.
Maria (People Ops): Ok — so practically, payroll needs to know whether we can set a start date that is "contingent" on having an acceptable I-9 document. What docs do we need to onboard her on 5/1 if EAD isn't in hand?
Ben (Payroll): For I-9, per the receipt rule, an EAD application receipt (I-797C for I-765) + a valid foreign passport might be accepted temporarily in List A for the 240-day rule. However, we need to confirm current guidance. If we can't accept that, they'd need an actual List A document (EAD) or a combination of List B+List C (work authorization + identity).
Sam (Benefits): For benefits enrollment, most carriers require a completed enrollment form plus an effective date tied to hire date. They don't typically require proof of work authorization at enrollment time, but eligibility for benefits (and payroll) hinges on valid employment authorization. Some carriers will flag if payroll is not set up. We can provisionally enroll and mark benefits effective date pending payroll verification, but need to be careful with dependent coverage / premium billing.
Maria (People Ops): Action items I'm thinking: 1) Priya to confirm whether the I-765 receipt will be acceptable for I-9 under current policy and whether we should expect the 240-day automatic work authorization. 2) Ben to outline payroll steps if we onboard under receipt rule (tax withholding, verification steps). 3) Sam to confirm whether we can do provisional benefits enrollment and retro-adjust premiums if EAD delays. 4) Ask candidate to upload receipts/docs to the secure onboarding portal.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): I'll check USCIS policy and past adjudication. Note: the receipt rule for automatic extension historically applied to timely-filed renewal EADs (switching employers) and some categories; for I-765 filed with I-485 concurrent filing, the 240-day provisional work authorization has been applied in many cases but it's best to treat it case-by-case. I'll confirm by EOD.
Arpita (Candidate): I'm going to upload the signed offer + copy of passport and will file I-485/I-765 on Monday. I'll share scans of the receipts here once I have them. Thanks all.
Maria (People Ops): Thanks. Please upload to the portal (link in DM) instead of slack. Also: flag whether you plan to be remote first 2 months or on-site — that affects I-9 timing (remote verification options vs in-person verification).
Arpita (Candidate): Likely remote first month, then relocate.
Ben (Payroll): If remote onboarding: we can use an authorized agent for in-person I-9 verification (per DHS guidance) or use remote electronic verification if allowed for the location. If the receipt rule applies, we still need to capture the receipt number and follow up when EAD arrives. We'll also need the candidate's SSN; if she doesn't have one yet we can issue a placeholder until SSA processes but reporting needs to be accurate for taxes.
Ash (Hiring Manager): Appreciate the details. From our side, we can set the start date to 2026-05-01 but mark 'contingent on acceptable work authorization' in Greenhouse/offers and ask People Ops to confirm 7 days before start.
Maria (People Ops): I'll add the contingency language and set a checkpoint 7 days prior. Also will add a checklist to the onboarding folder: (1) offer acceptance scanned, (2) passport, (3) I-485/I-765 receipts, (4) EAD when available, (5) SSN, (6) work location.
hr-bot: Reminder: Upload documents via secure HR portal only. Do not send PII over public channels.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Update: USCIS policy note — as of last internal check, the I-765 receipt for initial EADs with concurrent I-485 generally does not grant the automatic 240-day extension (that extension applies more clearly to renewal filings). That means receipt alone may not be sufficient for employers to rely on as authorization beyond an employer-specific discretionary acceptance. Recommend treating start as contingent unless candidate already has an EAD or other List A/C docs.
Ben (Payroll): Given Priya's update, payroll prefers we require one of: (A) existing valid EAD; (B) valid H-1B or other work visa; or (C) use List B+List C combo (but that still requires I-9 acceptable docs). If none are present, we can't pay someone not authorized. We can do a delayed start or contractor arrangement only after legal signs off — contractor setup has compliance implications.
Maria (People Ops): Thanks Priya & Ben. New plan: tell Arpita we love for her to start 5/1 but must present acceptable I-9 docs on or before that date (EAD or other). If she files I-765 and only has receipts, we will need legal to approve a case-by-case acceptance; otherwise push start until docs are in. Arpita, is that acceptable?
Arpita (Candidate): I understand. I'll prioritize filing and will update with receipts, but I may not have EAD by 5/1. If it's not possible I can delay start by a few weeks.
Ash (Hiring Manager): Fine from my side — we can delay 2–4 weeks if needed. Would prefer not to move further out.
Sam (Benefits): If start is delayed, benefits effective date will shift. If we do a provisional start and then EAD arrives, we can backdate coverage to start date once verification completed but only if premiums are managed correctly. I'll prepare an FAQ for Arpita about benefits timelines.
Maria (People Ops): I'll message Arpita the contingency language and checklist. Priya — please drop final confirmation on receipt rule and whether there's any employer guidance that allows temporary acceptance for concurrent I-485 I-765 receipts. Ben — please share payroll fallback options (contractor vs delayed hire) and any forms we'll need. Sam — please prepare benefits note.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Will do. ETA EOD.
Ben (Payroll): I'll draft two options and post them here by tomorrow morning.
Sam (Benefits): Will draft the FAQ and share before EOD as well.
Maria (People Ops): Great — thanks everyone. Arpita, feel free to ping me when receipts uploaded. :handshake:
Arpita (Candidate): Uploaded initial I-485/I-765 receipt PDF to portal. Thanks all.
Maria (People Ops): Got it — I'll queue legal review.
Priya (Immigration Counsel): Received receipts. Quick note after review: the receipt indicates category "C09" (adjustment applicant). Based on current guidance, I do not recommend relying on receipt-alone for payroll authorization. Recommend contingency continue.
Maria (People Ops): Understood. Arpita — would you like to keep 5/1 as tentative and target a soft start (no payroll) or push to 5/18 so payroll + benefits can go live on day one?
Arpita (Candidate): I'd prefer to delay to 5/18 to avoid complications. Sorry for the trouble.
Ash (Hiring Manager): 5/18 works. Welcome aboard — excited to have you! :tada:
